clue.text: Man in power-sharing arrangement with former dictator reveals Guardian

indicators.note: the sharing arrangement means the P ending the man word is also the start of the dictator, so it is written once

parts.note: Juan Perón was the former Argentine dictator
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A politician in a coalition deal with an ex-dictator reveals the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAP and PERON overlap on their shared P, giving CHAPERON.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies and supervises a young person, acting as their protector.

clue.text: Building American shed for garden

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so the building casts off the American

parts.note: US, the abbreviation for American, is removed

explanation.surface: Putting up a US-style shed at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like the garden building, but it is the verb meaning cast off; 'garden' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe is to work the soil with a long-handled weeding tool, one of the basic tasks of tending plants.

clue.text: Gather the nerve and plug our cupcake ingredients for a change

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are treated as ingredients to be mixed into something different

explanation.surface: A nervous baker steels themself to tamper with a cupcake recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ingredients' keeps the baking picture going while telling you the fodder's letters are to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for summoning bravery before doing something daunting.

clue.text: Artist laid back about copyright is ultimately sure to become more controversial

indicators.note: the turned-round 'laid' goes about, around, the abbreviation for copyright
'laid' taken back, written right to left, spells a new word

parts.note: the word itself, to be read backwards
the copyright symbol is a C in a circle

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of 'sure' is used

explanation.surface: A relaxed painter's attitude to copyright is bound to stir up controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' reads as relaxed, but it is LAID written backwards, DIAL, wrapped around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To radicalise is to adopt, or push someone to adopt, extreme political views, making them more contentious and divisive.

clue.text: Maybe go past an opponent in football season with this?

definitions.text: go past an opponent in football
definitions.meaning: in football slang, playing the ball through an opponent's legs and running round them
a spice grated over food to flavour it

explanation.surface: A question about what a footballer needs to beat defenders over a whole season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like the football calendar, but it is the cooking verb, to flavour food.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a cheeky dribbling trick through the legs and the aromatic seed used as a spice.

clue.text: Lose example of big road kill

parts.note: the M1 motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Losing track of an example of roadkill on a big road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road kill' pulls toward roadkill, but the words part: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, and 'kill' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it somewhere and then be unable to find it, a synonym of misplace.

clue.text: Rejecting some parliamentary post

indicators.note: rejecting sends something back, so the found letters are read in the other direction
only some of the next word's letters are wanted, a run inside it

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Someone turning down a job in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job, as in a parliamentary post, but it is the letters delivered to your door.
explanation.definitionFit: Post and mail are synonyms for letters and parcels delivered by the postal service.

clue.text: Hurt leg, say cycling within group creating problem

indicators.note: within means the cycled letters sit inside the other word
cycling means letters are moved round from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: a leg is an example of a limb
a block is a group, as in a block of seats

explanation.surface: An injured leg keeps a cyclist in the bunch, which causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like riding a bike, and 'group' like a cycling bunch; instead it signals letters moved round from the front of the word to its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumbling block is an obstacle that holds up progress, so it is a problem.

clue.text: Number ten is a cheat, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together by some unspecified rearrangement

explanation.surface: An accusation that the number ten, perhaps a footballer, is somehow a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure like ten, but it is NUMB-ER, something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic is a drug that removes sensation, so it literally makes a patient numb.

clue.text: Prolific in French, occasionally and in German

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who is productive when speaking French now and then, and German too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' seems to modify how often French is spoken, but it picks odd letters from the word French itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecund means fertile and highly productive, able to produce offspring or ideas in abundance.

clue.text: Fish bone inside loaf initially leads to court

indicators.note: the bone goes inside the fish
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of 'loaf' counts

explanation.surface: A fishbone found in a loaf ends up in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: The bone goes inside after the first letter of TUNA, and L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body appointed to judge disputes, a kind of law court.

clue.text: Psychedelic rock band on front of stage for opener

indicators.note: psychedelic means wildly distorted, so the letters of rock are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: front of means the first letter

parts.note: a crew is a band of people

explanation.surface: A trippy rock group plays at the front of the stage as the support act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like the first act on a bill; it is a tool for opening bottles. 'Psychedelic' turns ROCK into CORK.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the tool used to pull the cork from a bottle of wine, so it is a bottle opener.

clue.text: Taylor finally in line for game of darts — set out to secure right score

indicators.note: Taylor's letter goes in the darts line

parts.note: the oche is the line darts players stand behind to throw

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the name Taylor
to secure is to hold fast, so 'set out' holds 'right'

parts.note: to set out a case is to state it

explanation.surface: Phil Taylor, the darts champion, finally at the line in a game, sets out to hit the right score.
explanation.walkthrough: Phil Taylor is a famous darts champion, which makes 'score' look like darts points; it is the musical verb, to arrange for an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a piece of music is to arrange it for the instruments of an orchestra, which is exactly what orchestrating means.

clue.text: Humble sailor sea swimming

indicators.note: things swimming move about, so the letters of 'sea' move into a new order

explanation.surface: A modest sailor out swimming in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' looks like an adjective describing the sailor, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to lower them in dignity or esteem, so to humble or humiliate them.

clue.text: The Police out on tour at last — it might take off

indicators.note: out suggests the band's name is knocked out of shape and rearranged
at last points to the closing letter of the word tour

explanation.surface: The rock band The Police back out on tour at last, and it might be a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Police were Sting's band; 'take off' looks like a success, but it means leave the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is an aircraft that lifts vertically into the air, so it is something that literally takes off.

clue.text: Two partners in firm using prime locations exclusively for introductions

indicators.note: introductions are openings, so each of the four words gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Two partners in a firm that trades only from the best sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime locations' sounds like property, and 'prime' might tempt you to take prime-numbered letters; the first letters of four words are what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair of people in a relationship, two people joined as partners.

clue.text: See 3
Sunak briefly embracing Musk without touching stomach

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so the shortened first name wraps around Musk's
briefly means cut short, so the ex-prime minister's first name loses its final letter

parts.note: Rishi Sunak, the former UK prime minister

indicators.note: without means lacking, so Musk's first name drops the word for touching

parts.note: on can mean touching, as a cup on a table

explanation.surface: Rishi Sunak briefly hugs Elon Musk while avoiding touching his belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like a noun, the belly, but it is the verb to tolerate. RISH wraps EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomach as a verb means to tolerate or like; relish means to enjoy, and 'not relish' and 'not stomach' are close idioms.

clue.text: Musk's company invested in city with tightwad eschewing banks and tax

indicators.note: invested in means put inside

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
X is the social media company Elon Musk owns, formerly Twitter

indicators.note: eschewing banks means losing the letters at both edges

explanation.surface: A billionaire's firm puts money into the City alongside a skinflint dodging banks and taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests finance, but it means the edges of the miser. The City is the City of London, whose postcode area is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a duty charged on goods such as alcohol and tobacco, a form of tax.

clue.text: Comic holding in good ad-lib

indicators.note: to hold is to have inside, so the comic has 'in good' inside

parts.note: a wit is a comic person

explanation.surface: A comedian who, when in good form, improvises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding in' reads as a single phrase, but 'in' belongs with 'good' as the contents.
explanation.definitionFit: To wing it is an idiom meaning to improvise without preparation, which is what ad-libbing is.

clue.text: The morning's breaking over source of Snake River

indicators.note: the morning breaks into the middle of 'The', splitting it
a river's source is where it starts, so the start of the word snake

explanation.surface: Dawn breaking over the source of the Snake River in the American northwest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Snake River is a real US river, so 'Snake River' reads as one name; 'River' alone is the definition. In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river that flows through London, a well-known example of the class.

clue.text: Small market for drink

parts.note: S, the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to tout is to market or sell something

explanation.surface: A small market stall selling beverages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Market' looks like a noun but is the verb to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout is a strong dark beer, such as Guinness, one example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: A more primitive type of project getting support

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned kind of project finding backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' is the verb, pronounced with the stress on the second syllable, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwback is something that reverts to an earlier ancestral form or style, an atavism.

clue.text: See 7
Very small object in your trousers

indicators.note: the letters sit in the run of words that follow, across their breaks

parts.note: the end of one word, a whole short word, and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a small object in someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'in' also forms part of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a straightforward synonym for minute or minuscule, extremely little.

clue.text: Model soldier first to march on trench

parts.note: a dig is an excavation, a trench

indicators.note: the first of the word march is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A model soldier is the first to march into the trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model soldier' reads as one ideal soldier, or a toy one; 'Model' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a typical example or pattern of something, an exemplar.

clue.text: Group of performers using figure of speech to inspire you in audition

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the figure of speech takes the letter inside

parts.note: a trope is a figure of speech

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter name sounds like the pronoun

explanation.surface: A theatre company using a stirring turn of phrase to motivate you at a casting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' fits the performers but signals a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of actors, dancers or entertainers who tour or work together.

clue.text: It might be used to fry prawns every now and then

definitions.text: It might be used to fry

indicators.note: at intervals, so every other letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A kitchen question about what is occasionally used to fry prawns.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of use, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying pan is the shallow metal cooking vessel used for frying food over heat.

clue.text: As a result of this blasphemy making second book

indicators.note: making here means turning into, so the letter for second becomes the letter for book

parts.note: heresy is blasphemy, an offence against religious doctrine

explanation.surface: A blasphemous act inspires a sequel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second book' looks like a sequel; really the S of HERESY is replaced by B.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereby is a formal adverb meaning by means of this document or statement, as in legal wording.

clue.text: Beautiful out

definitions.meaning: workers who are out have walked out in an industrial dispute

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is the trade-union sense: workers who are 'out' have downed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking means both impressively attractive and taking part in a strike, withdrawing labour from an employer.
